topic_groups.topic: Nutrition, Diet, Weight and Metabolic Health

articles.title: Health Benefits of a Mediterranean Diet
articles.summary_3_sentences: A recent study highlights reported positive effects of a Mediterranean diet on heart health. The provided record does not include details on study design or population.

articles.title: Low-fat vegan diet cuts dietary energy density by nearly a third, helping explain weight loss
articles.summary_3_sentences: New research in JAMA Network Open reports that a low-fat vegan diet lowered dietary energy density by about 30%. The authors suggest this may help people lose weight while eating satisfying amounts of food without intentionally restricting calories.

articles.title: Wine, beer, or spirits? Massive study finds a surprising health divide
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study following more than 340,000 adults found heavy drinking was linked to higher mortality regardless of beverage type. At lower levels, beer, cider and spirits were linked to higher mortality, while wine consumption was associated with lower cardiovascular death risk.

articles.title: For decades, we were told to choose low-fat dairy. New research says otherwise
articles.summary_3_sentences: A 12-week study found that adults eating three daily servings of full-fat dairy did not show meaningful increases in weight, body fat, cholesterol or insulin resistance. Participants also had improved blood pressure and higher intake of calcium, protein and vitamin D.

articles.title: Cutting sweet foods doesn't curb cravings or improve health
articles.summary_3_sentences: A six-month trial found no meaningful differences in sweetness preference, body weight or cardiometabolic markers among people assigned to high-, low- or average-sweetness diets. Many participants also drifted back toward previous eating habits after the trial.

articles.title: Scientists reveal how much exercise you really need to protect your heart
articles.summary_3_sentences: A large study suggests that 150 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous weekly exercise may provide only modest protection against heart attacks and strokes. The largest benefits were associated with much higher activity levels, roughly 560 to 610 minutes per week.

articles.title: Your brain may be wired to regain lost weight
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article describes biological mechanisms that may drive weight regain after dieting, including increased hunger, cravings and lower energy use. It notes that medications such as Wegovy and Mounjaro can reduce appetite signals, though effects may fade after treatment stops.

articles.title: This once-a-week workout may help cut belly fat, study shows
articles.summary_3_sentences: A four-month trial in 315 adults with central obesity found that one weekly 75-minute brisk interval walking session reduced body fat and waist size. The results were similar to splitting the same exercise across three days.

articles.title: Eating less protein could slow aging, major review finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: A review of more than 350 studies suggests that lower protein intake may improve metabolic and inflammatory markers linked to healthier aging. The article frames the findings as a challenge to high-protein dietary trends.

articles.title: Eating one avocado a day may lower heart disease risk
articles.summary_3_sentences: A six-month study in adults with obesity found that eating one avocado daily reduced circulating LDL particle numbers. The reported change was associated with an estimated 4% reduction in cardiovascular risk.

articles.title: Experts say blood pressure guidelines are missing half the equation
articles.summary_3_sentences: A new report argues that blood pressure control should focus on increasing potassium as well as reducing sodium. Potassium-rich foods may help counter sodium's effects, but typical intake remains below recommendations.

articles.title: Popular Childhood Drinks May Cause High Blood Pressure Later in Life
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports a link between sugary drink consumption in childhood and higher blood pressure risk later in life. It emphasizes reducing sugary beverages in youth as a possible cardiovascular prevention strategy.

articles.title: A 42-year-old childhood obesity theory may be wrong
articles.summary_3_sentences: New research challenges the idea that BMI increases around age 6 reflect an adiposity rebound. A more direct measure suggested body fat did not rebound, and the BMI change may reflect growth in lean tissue.

articles.title: Rice bran compound may help ease irritable bowel symptoms
articles.summary_3_sentences: Laboratory experiments found that ferulic acid from rice bran reduced calcium signaling involved in intestinal muscle contraction. The finding could inform future dietary approaches for diarrhea-related digestive disorders, though it may not suit constipation.

articles.title: New microwave frying method could make french fries much healthier
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers propose combining microwave heating with conventional frying to make fries crisp while reducing oil absorption. The approach is presented as a food-processing strategy rather than a clinical intervention.

articles.title: Daily multivitamin may help older adults stay independent
articles.summary_3_sentences: A preliminary three-year study found that older adults taking a daily multivitamin reported better functional health than those receiving placebo. The findings still require peer review.

articles.title: Misfolded insulin may be quietly driving diabetes
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that insulin-producing cells rely on helper proteins to maintain insulin production. When one partner was missing, damaged proteins accumulated and insulin output fell, suggesting a possible pancreatic protection strategy.

articles.title: Eating within 8 hours may help keep the aging brain sharp
articles.summary_3_sentences: A small six-month trial found that older women who limited eating to about 8 to 9 hours daily performed better on planning and problem-solving tests. Weight loss was similar across groups, suggesting timing may matter beyond calories.

articles.title: Scientists reveal what sparkling water really does to your teeth
articles.summary_3_sentences: A small preliminary study found unsweetened sparkling water caused only a temporary salivary pH drop compared with soda. The acidity remained above the level associated with enamel damage.

articles.title: Why losing the wrong fat can trigger diabetes
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that damaged fat cells can become inflamed, lose lipid-storage capacity and disappear. The findings suggest diabetes can arise from loss of healthy fat tissue as well as from excess fat.

articles.title: Your AI calorie-tracking app may be off by 345 calories
articles.summary_3_sentences: Four AI-powered food apps underestimated calories and fat by about one-third when tested against prepared meals. High-fat ketogenic dishes were especially difficult for the apps to measure accurately.

articles.title: Oral GLP-1 drugs may quiet the brain's food craving circuit
articles.summary_3_sentences: In mice, newer oral drugs related to semaglutide reduced pleasure-driven eating by affecting a deep brain reward circuit. The findings are preclinical and may inform research on cravings and substance use disorder.

articles.title: GLP-1 Drugs Could Help Slow Some Aging Processes
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reviews evidence that GLP-1 agonists such as Ozempic and Wegovy may influence metabolic pathways tied to aging. It frames these possible effects as emerging and beyond established weight-management uses.

articles.title: The billion-dollar problem keeping Ozempic, Wegovy, and Zepbound from patients
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers report that GLP-1 weight-loss drugs may offer strong health value but could strain insurance budgets if widely covered. The article also warns about safety risks from low-cost compounded versions.

articles.title: Coffee may protect your heart but energy drinks could harm it
articles.summary_3_sentences: An American Heart Association review reports that up to 400 mg of caffeine daily is generally safe for most adults and may be linked to lower cardiometabolic risks. Highly concentrated energy drinks and shots may raise blood pressure and trigger irregular rhythms.

articles.title: Artificial Sweeteners May Impair the Growth of Gut Microbes
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports findings that artificial sweeteners can hinder growth of beneficial gut bacteria. It raises concerns about possible effects on microbial diversity.

articles.title: Popular sugar substitutes linked to faster brain aging
articles.summary_3_sentences: Adults with the highest intake of several artificial sweeteners showed faster declines in memory and thinking, especially under age 60 or with diabetes. Researchers emphasized that more studies are needed before inferring causation.

articles.title: Scientists tested 39 sweeteners and found unexpected gut effects
articles.summary_3_sentences: A large laboratory study found that many sweeteners directly altered gut bacterial growth. Researchers also identified more than 100 interactions involving sweeteners combined with medications, caffeine or flavorings.

articles.title: Mediterranean diet may activate tiny proteins that protect the heart and brain
articles.summary_3_sentences: Older adults who followed a Mediterranean diet more closely had higher levels of mitochondrial peptides linked to heart and brain protection. Olive oil, fish, legumes and lower refined carbohydrate intake appeared especially relevant.

articles.title: Popular weight-loss drugs Ozempic and Wegovy may slow biological aging
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that semaglutide slowed biological aging markers in adults with HIV. The article notes this is early clinical evidence and larger studies are needed before concluding the drug slows aging.

articles.title: Chewing bubble gum after beetroot may help lower blood pressure
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study found that chewing sugary gum after nitrate-rich vegetables or beetroot juice increased beneficial nitrite production and temporarily lowered blood pressure. Researchers hope to identify healthier ways to enhance nitrate-related cardiovascular benefits.

articles.title: Experimental drug reverses severe fatty liver disease by repairing the gut
articles.summary_3_sentences: In animal studies, an experimental drug called DT-109 reversed severe fatty liver disease by repairing the gut and reducing harmful liver-directed toxins. The findings are preclinical and point to possible treatments for MASH.

articles.title: Dense breasts or breast cancer in the family? What screening changes mean for you
articles.summary_3_sentences: A review in Australia supports moving breast cancer screening away from age-based criteria alone. The proposed approach would tailor screening based on individual risk factors such as dense breasts and family history.

articles.title: Protein 'switch' determines whether liposarcoma cells will become aggressive
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified a protein switch that appears to influence whether liposarcoma cells become more aggressive. The work points to possible targets for keeping aggressive tumors in check.

articles.title: Study points to new target for treating aggressive brain cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified SET as a potential target for glioblastoma treatment. The work suggests targeting SET could make glioblastoma cells more vulnerable to radiation and chemotherapy.

articles.title: Two-stage process helps metastatic cancer cells hide, then multiply in the lungs
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Science study mapped how some cancer cells survive after reaching the lungs despite immune elimination of many metastatic cells. The article describes a two-stage process in which cells first hide and later multiply.

articles.title: Protective drug dexrazoxane reduces heart damage in pediatric cancer survivors years after treatment ends
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study found that dexrazoxane reduced chemotherapy-related heart damage in pediatric cancer survivors 15 years or more after treatment. The findings support long-term cardioprotective benefits in this population.

articles.title: High glucose thickens cancer cells' sugar shield, helping them evade immune attack
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers report that high glucose can thicken sugar-derived coatings on cancer cells. The mechanism may help tumors evade immune detection, though the record does not specify clinical testing.

articles.title: Radiopharmaceutical may benefit patients with metastatic prostate cancer sooner
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Phase III trial found that earlier use of targeted radionuclide therapy delayed progression in metastatic prostate cancer when used as part of a three-drug regimen. The trial involved investigators from multiple institutions worldwide.

articles.title: D-serine accelerates gastric tumor growth by suppressing killer T cells
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that D-serine can accelerate gastric tumor growth by suppressing killer T-cell activity. The findings relate to immune evasion mechanisms that may affect responses to checkpoint inhibitors.

articles.title: Scientists finally crack nature's secret for building better cancer drugs
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified how bacteria naturally produce multiple versions of anti-cancer compounds. The discovery could help engineers create improved nature-inspired cancer drugs.

articles.title: A protein older than blood circulation could transform cancer immunotherapy
articles.summary_3_sentences: In mice, tumor-produced C3 blocked immune-suppressing cells and improved immunotherapy responses. Researchers recreated the effect in resistant tumors and reported improved survival in the preclinical models.

articles.title: Vitamin C may fight cancer -- but not the way scientists once thought
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article distinguishes ordinary oral vitamin C supplements from high-dose intravenous vitamin C, which reaches much higher concentrations. Early studies suggest intravenous vitamin C may affect vulnerable cancer cells or treatment side effects, but the evidence remains developing.

articles.title: Cancer-fighting chewing gum cuts HPV levels by up to 93%
articles.summary_3_sentences: An engineered chewing gum reduced HPV levels by up to 93% and nearly eliminated two bacteria linked to head and neck cancer. The treatment also preserved beneficial oral bacteria in the reported study.

articles.title: A common sugar may help cancer cells break free and spread
articles.summary_3_sentences: The study suggests chemotherapy-surviving ovarian cancer cells may release fructose that helps nearby tumor cells loosen and spread. The article notes that dietary and drug-related implications have not been confirmed in patients.

articles.title: A simple supplement could help the immune system fight cancer and viruses
articles.summary_3_sentences: In mice, arginine-rich diets were linked to fewer colon tumors and milder viral infections. The findings suggest arginine may affect immune warning pathways, but translation to humans remains unproven.

articles.title: Cancer may be breaking its own DNA to keep growing
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers report that intense activity at cancer growth switches can damage tumor DNA. Repeated repair may introduce mutations that help tumors evolve, potentially revealing a therapeutic vulnerability.

articles.title: Blood cancer's genetic warning signs may appear years early
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that blood cancers that later worsen may carry detectable genetic warning signs years before severe symptoms. The findings may help distinguish dangerous disease from harmless age-related blood changes.

articles.title: Healthy pregnancies and newborns are possible after CAR T cell therapy
articles.summary_3_sentences: Women treated with CAR T cell therapy for autoimmune diseases later had regular pregnancies and healthy babies. The record suggests pregnancy after CAR T therapy may be possible, though detailed study size is not provided.

articles.title: Why the same DNA damage causes cancer in some people but not others
articles.summary_3_sentences: A controlled mouse study found that inherited genetics can shape how cancer begins and evolves after DNA damage. The work may eventually inform personalized cancer risk prediction and screening.

articles.title: CRISPR makes prostate cancer vulnerable to immunotherapy
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists used CRISPR to make prostate cancer cells easier for the immune system to detect. In mice, the experimental approach improved immunotherapy effects.

articles.title: New cancer strategy could stop tumors before resistance takes hold
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers are applying evolutionary theory to cancer treatment by switching therapies before tumors develop resistance. Mathematical models suggest rapid, carefully timed multi-therapy switches could improve cure rates.

articles.title: This sugar-coated therapy boosted survival against deadly brain cancer by 50% in mice
articles.summary_3_sentences: In mice, sugar-coated nanoparticles delivered genetic instructions to restore a tumor-suppressing protein in glioblastoma cells. The preclinical therapy increased median survival by 50% and shrank tumors without reported organ damage.

articles.title: This pet gecko could help scientists unlock the secrets of cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists identified a leopard gecko that naturally develops aggressive tumors as a potential cancer research model. Its tumors share key genetic changes with human cancers.

articles.title: Common blood pressure drug could make cancer therapy far more powerful
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that telmisartan may improve the anticancer effects of olaparib, potentially expanding its use beyond BRCA-related tumors. The combination showed immune-boosting and anticancer effects in preclinical studies and is being tested in human trials.

topic_groups.topic: Neurology, Alzheimer's Disease and Brain Aging

articles.title: Early Alzheimer's patients pursuing lecanemab show low adherence to brain health advice
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found poor adherence to 15 brain health recommendations among patients with early Alzheimer's disease. Fewer than 3% followed all recommendations, with no significant difference between those pursuing lecanemab and those not pursuing anti-amyloid therapy.

articles.title: Parkinson's-linked α-synuclein blocks protein transport in neurons, disrupting cells' waste recycling
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers report that toxic forms of alpha-synuclein can block protein transport in neurons. The mechanism may disrupt cellular waste recycling and help explain neuronal dysfunction in Parkinson's disease.

articles.title: Scientists discover a hidden brain shift that begins around age 50
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that around age 50, the brain's memory center may lose many resident immune cells and replace them with more inflammatory ones. This shift may help explain how normal aging increases vulnerability to dementia.

articles.title: Nearly half of dementia cases may be linked to risks you can change
articles.summary_3_sentences: A long-term brain study linked smoking, high blood pressure, heart disease and high blood lipids to damage associated with vascular dementia. The findings suggest modifiable risks may contribute substantially to dementia burden.

articles.title: Two new compounds could reveal hidden drivers of Alzheimer's disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: Vanderbilt researchers developed a selective TAOK-1 inhibitor and a second compound that activates the TAOK protein family. These tools may help reveal Alzheimer's disease mechanisms and guide treatment research.

articles.title: Scientists may have found aging's hidden trigger for brain disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: In worms, the protein EPS8 accumulated with age and promoted toxic protein clumping linked to neurodegeneration. Reducing EPS8 prevented aggregates and preserved nerve function in the model.

articles.title: AI can tell if your brain is aging faster than you are
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers used machine learning on EEG recordings from about 7,000 adults to estimate sleep-based brain age. An older-than-expected brain age was associated with higher dementia risk.

articles.title: Scientists discover why poor sleep may harm some brains more
articles.summary_3_sentences: A gene involved in the brain's overnight cleaning system may influence how poor sleep affects Alzheimer's-related brain changes. The findings suggest prevention strategies may need to consider both genetics and sleep habits.

articles.title: Scientists discover how obesity may fuel Alzheimer's disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified a possible pathway linking obesity to Alzheimer's disease through fat molecules that affect brain immune defenses and amyloid buildup. Correcting the fat imbalance improved memory and brain function in Alzheimer's models.

articles.title: What if the brain does not create consciousness?
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article describes Christof Koch's work on the hard problem of consciousness and whether the brain creates conscious experience. It discusses topics such as near-death experiences and terminal lucidity as part of a broader theoretical inquiry.

articles.title: Genomic Mapping Opens a New Frontier in Alzheimer's
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that genomic mapping has identified new genetic regions associated with Alzheimer's disease. These discoveries may expand understanding of disease biology and future diagnostic or therapeutic development.

articles.title: A hidden Alzheimer's tipping point may decide who gets dementia
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists identified a possible tipping point in how brain immune cells respond to Alzheimer's plaques and tau. The mechanism may help explain why some people develop dementia and could provide a treatment target.

articles.title: Superagers keep youthful memories but their DNA does not explain why
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that SuperAgers did not simply carry fewer Alzheimer's-related genetic risks than typical older adults. Their exceptional memory may depend on still-unknown protective factors involving biology, lifestyle or environment.

articles.title: APOE2 may protect the brain from Alzheimer's and aging
articles.summary_3_sentences: The APOE2 gene variant appears to protect brain cells by reducing DNA damage and helping neurons recover from stress. The finding could inspire therapies that mimic APOE2's protective effects.

articles.title: Lab-grown mini brains may predict which Alzheimer's treatments will work
articles.summary_3_sentences: Patient-derived brain organoids showed different responses to an antidepressant in Alzheimer's-related tissue models. The organoids and particles they release may eventually support personalized treatment research.

articles.title: Watching too much TV in midlife may shrink the brain
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study of about 1,700 adults linked frequent midlife television viewing with smaller brain regions and more white matter damage decades later. The association appeared distinct from sitting itself, because mentally engaging seated work was linked to healthier patterns.

articles.title: Alzheimer's breakthrough: Scientists restore two hours of sleep without clearing brain plaques
articles.summary_3_sentences: In mice with amyloid plaques, overactive microglia drove inflammation linked to loss of deep sleep. Temporarily removing most microglia restored more than two hours of sleep per day without clearing plaques.

articles.title: Scientists Learn More About the Genetic Basis of Epilepsy
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports identification of additional genetic factors underlying epilepsy. These findings may improve understanding of molecular causes and support future diagnostic or treatment strategies.

articles.title: Scientists discover a protein that protects the brain from Alzheimer's damage
articles.summary_3_sentences: In mice, extra SORLA was linked to less tau accumulation, less brain atrophy and healthier neuronal connections. The findings suggest SORLA-related pathways may protect against Alzheimer's-type damage.

articles.title: Genes offer new clues to stopping Huntington's disease in its tracks
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article describes emerging therapies aimed at intervening between Huntington's molecular progression and neurological consequences. It focuses on gene-related strategies for slowing or preventing disease effects.

articles.title: The hidden skeleton "gatekeeper" inside brain cells could help fight Alzheimer's
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that a microscopic neuronal skeleton controls what brain cells absorb and when. When weakened, neurons rapidly took up harmful Alzheimer's-associated proteins, suggesting stabilization could be protective.

articles.title: Alzheimer's tau protein has a surprising secret role in memory
articles.summary_3_sentences: A mouse study found that tau helps convert new experiences into lasting memories by organizing memory-storing cells. Abnormal tau may disrupt both memory formation and recall in Alzheimer's disease.

articles.title: New Alzheimer's drug repairs DNA damage and reduces brain inflammation
articles.summary_3_sentences: In mouse studies, KCL-286 repaired DNA damage, reduced inflammation and targeted multiple Alzheimer's-related pathways. The drug has already cleared an initial human safety trial for another indication.

articles.title: Yale scientists may have found how Parkinson's disease spreads through the brain
articles.summary_3_sentences: Yale researchers identified two neuron surface proteins that appear to help spread toxic Parkinson's-linked protein. Blocking them in mice reduced disease progression, suggesting a potential therapeutic target.

topic_groups.topic: Mental Health, Behavior, Sleep and Cognition

articles.title: New targeting method separates opioid pain relief from reward learning in mice
articles.summary_3_sentences: Duke researchers report a mouse study aimed at preserving opioid pain relief while reducing reward learning linked to addiction risk. The work is preclinical and was published in Nature.

articles.title: What is emotional regulation? A child psychologist explains
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article explains emotional regulation as a long-studied psychological concept rather than a social media buzzword. It is an expert explainer focused on child psychology and mental health.

articles.title: Frequent cannabis users wake up with their "stress hormone" already elevated
articles.summary_3_sentences: Frequent cannabis users were reported to wake with unusually high cortisol levels. Researchers say the finding raises questions about whether repeated cannabis use for stress relief may disrupt stress-response rhythms.

articles.title: ADHD diagnoses and prescriptions have increased globally across all age groups, our review shows
articles.summary_3_sentences: A review found that ADHD diagnoses have increased in many countries across all age groups. Prescriptions for ADHD treatments have risen in parallel.

articles.title: Study reveals prefrontal cortex can hinder learning more efficient behaviors
articles.summary_3_sentences: A mouse study found that the prefrontal cortex can sometimes interfere with learning more efficient behaviors. The finding challenges a simple view of the region as always supporting flexible learning.

articles.title: Scientists say just 7 days of meditation can rewire your brain
articles.summary_3_sentences: An intensive seven-day meditation retreat was linked to changes in brain and body measures related to neuroplasticity, immunity, metabolism and natural pain relief. Participants also showed connectivity patterns resembling those associated with psychedelic experiences.

articles.title: Stress can scramble your brain's internal GPS, MRI study finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: An MRI study found that cortisol made participants worse at navigating a virtual environment and disrupted grid-cell activity. Another brain region appeared to compensate when landmarks were missing.

articles.title: Psychedelics amplify brain connectivity through serotonin receptors, study suggests
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses research on how psychedelics alter perception, thought and consciousness through serotonin receptors. It emphasizes basic mechanisms rather than only potential psychiatric treatment effects.

articles.title: 'Mindfulness-based cognitive therapy' may reduce internet gaming disorder in college students
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers developed a Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy for Gaming program for college students with internet gaming disorder. The study found promising evidence of therapeutic effectiveness.

articles.title: Teen cannabis use linked to slower memory and thinking growth
articles.summary_3_sentences: Teen cannabis use was linked to slower growth in memory, attention, language and processing speed. THC was identified as the most likely driver, especially for memory changes.

articles.title: Scientists tracked 12 people in Antarctica for 10 months--what happened could shape future Mars missions
articles.summary_3_sentences: A 10-month Antarctic study of 12 people found that frequent contact with the same people was linked to tension and mistrust. The crew increasingly divided into cultural and language-based groups, with implications for long-duration space missions.

articles.title: Wearable ultrasound patch boosts REM sleep without drugs or surgery
articles.summary_3_sentences: In a study of 28 participants, a wearable ultrasound patch shortened time to REM sleep and increased REM duration. Researchers also observed signs of altered stress regulation and emotion-related brain circuits.

articles.title: New autism therapy shows surprising benefits even in adult mice
articles.summary_3_sentences: Blocking the glycine transporter SLC6A20 improved social, communication and repetitive behaviors in autism-related mouse models. The treatment also worked in human brain organoids, but clinical relevance remains unproven.

articles.title: THC medication made PTSD nightmares disappear for more than a third of patients
articles.summary_3_sentences: A prescription form of THC reduced recurring PTSD nightmares, with more than one-third of patients reporting complete disappearance after 10 weeks. The article presents the findings as a possible treatment direction for a difficult symptom.

articles.title: Scientists discover the brain cells that keep you motivated
articles.summary_3_sentences: In rats, orexin neurons helped sustain effort when reaching a reward became harder. Blocking these cells reduced motivation, suggesting a possible target for studying goal-directed behavior.

articles.title: Sitting up straight may improve your mood and decision-making
articles.summary_3_sentences: Participants who sat upright reported more pride and took more successful risks in a virtual balloon task than those who hunched. The study suggests posture may subtly affect mood and decision-making.

articles.title: Scientists find a simple routine linked to less pain and depression
articles.summary_3_sentences: Consistent daily routines for waking, eating, socializing and sleeping were linked to less pain and depression, especially in older adults with insomnia. Researchers suggest routines may strengthen circadian rhythms.

articles.title: Can't sleep in the heat? These 8 tricks could save your night
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article gives practical advice for sleeping during heatwaves, including blocking sunlight, ventilating at cooler times and using fans or ice packs safely. It focuses on reducing home overheating and improving comfort.

articles.title: Single Drug Dose Reversed Autism-Like Traits in Mice
articles.summary_3_sentences: A single dose of rapamycin temporarily reversed autism-like brain dysfunction and behavior in adult mice. The findings are preclinical and provide insight into neural pathways associated with autism.

articles.title: Your dreams aren't random. Your brain is rewriting reality
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study of more than 3,700 dream and waking reports found dreams reflect both personality and surrounding context. The dreaming brain appears to combine memories, emotions, possibilities and familiar settings rather than simply replaying daily events.

articles.title: A single dose reversed autism-like symptoms in adult mice within hours
articles.summary_3_sentences: In mice, prenatal inflammation led to persistent brain overactivity, sensory sensitivity, repetitive behaviors and increased seizure risk. One dose of rapamycin temporarily improved many of these problems within about two hours.

articles.title: Magic mushrooms may reshape the brain long after the trip ends
articles.summary_3_sentences: A single psilocybin dose produced measurable brain activity changes and possible structural changes lasting up to a month. Participants with greater increases in flexible brain activity reported more insight and later well-being improvements.

articles.title: Common antidepressant may ease long COVID's crushing fatigue
articles.summary_3_sentences: A randomized trial of 399 adults found that fluvoxamine reduced long COVID fatigue and improved quality of life compared with placebo. The article describes it as one of the first medications to show meaningful benefits for this symptom.

articles.title: Common constipation drug may help clear depression brain fog
articles.summary_3_sentences: In a small clinical trial, people with a history of depression performed better on memory, attention and thinking-speed tests after about a week of prucalopride than after placebo. The drug targets a serotonin receptor found in the gut and brain.

articles.title: Scientists discovered the brain doesn't make decisions the way we thought
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study suggests primary sensory regions are rapidly influenced by higher brain areas during decision-making. This challenges a simple feed-forward model and may inform future low-power AI systems.

articles.title: Scientists discover how the brain rewires itself to truly multitask
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that extensive training reorganizes brain circuits so learned tasks can bypass the prefrontal cortex. This may free cognitive resources and improve performance on a second task.

articles.title: Second pregnancy changes the brain in surprising new ways
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that each pregnancy rewires the brain differently, with a second pregnancy producing a pattern distinct from the first. The work may inform recognition and treatment of maternal mental health challenges.

topic_groups.topic: Infectious Disease, Vaccines and Antimicrobial Resistance

articles.title: New study finds bacterial infections affect about 1 in 20 hospitalized adults with firearm injuries
articles.summary_3_sentences: A University of Maryland study found bacterial infections in about 5% of adults hospitalized with firearm injuries. Most infections occurred during the initial hospitalization rather than after discharge.

articles.title: AI-designed E. coli killer points toward new ways to fight antibiotic-resistant bacteria
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers are using AI to engineer bacteriophage DNA as a possible strategy against antibiotic-resistant bacteria. The article focuses on an AI-designed phage approach targeting E. coli.

articles.title: Malaria vaccine add-ons activate three antibody targets, study finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that malaria vaccine add-ons can activate antibodies against three targets. The work aims to improve on WHO-recommended RTS,S and R21 vaccines, which provide useful but limited protection.

articles.title: A Working Antibacterial Resistance Gene is Found in Nature
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers discovered a functional antibacterial resistance gene occurring naturally. The finding highlights environmental reservoirs that may contribute to antibiotic resistance.

articles.title: A new antiviral could stop measles before an outbreak takes off
articles.summary_3_sentences: An experimental pill prevented a measles-like virus from spreading through air or close contact in ferrets. It worked around the time of exposure and shortened illness and contagiousness in the animal model.

articles.title: Measles cases in the U.S. hit a new 34-year high
articles.summary_3_sentences: Science News reports that U.S. measles cases reached their highest number since 1992. An epidemiologist explains factors driving the surge.

articles.title: Scientists revive a powerful antibiotic that superbugs had defeated
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers paired vancomycin with pghi-4, a small molecule that blocks a bacterial resistance-related enzyme. The combination restored activity against drug-resistant E. faecium in the reported work.

articles.title: An experimental oral vaccine may prevent invasive bacterial diarrhea
articles.summary_3_sentences: An experimental oral vaccine protected adults against Shigella in a small human trial. Shigella causes hundreds of thousands of U.S. infections annually.

articles.title: New molecular map reveals how the flu virus hijacks human cells
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists mapped how influenza A commandeers human cells, including a strategy involving nuclear structures. The map may reveal drug targets and help research on dangerous flu strains such as H5N1.

articles.title: A Novel Pathway Boosts COVID-19 & Drives Lung Damage
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports a pathway that may enhance SARS-CoV-2 effects and contribute to lung damage. Understanding the mechanism could inform therapeutic research.

articles.title: This food compound may help vaccines work better in older adults
articles.summary_3_sentences: In a small pilot trial, spermidine supplements after a third COVID-19 vaccine dose improved some immune responses in adults over 65. The largest benefits appeared among initially poor responders.

articles.title: Inside the fight against the parasite Cyclospora
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports on Cyclospora-related diarrheal illness in the United States. It notes that containing the outbreak is challenging.

articles.title: Tiny plastics in drinking water may be making dangerous bacteria stronger
articles.summary_3_sentences: Research suggests nanoplastics in drinking water can strengthen bacterial biofilms in water systems. Tougher biofilms may become more resistant to disinfectants and harder to remove.

articles.title: Scientists finally solved why some frogs survive a deadly fungus
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that some frogs develop strong immune defenses as tadpoles before exposure to a deadly fungus after metamorphosis. The study also identified many antimicrobial peptides that could inspire future infection research.

topic_groups.topic: Cardiovascular, Kidney, Public Health and Health Policy

articles.title: Expert comment: How do wildfires affect health and what can be done about it?
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses health effects of wildfires during a severe northern hemisphere fire season. It notes major burned areas, drought conditions and the need for health-related responses.

articles.title: AI could help Medicaid enrollees meet 80-hour work rules
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article examines how AI could help implement Medicaid work requirements as states prepare for new rules. It frames the issue as a complex health policy and administrative challenge.

articles.title: Social prescribing boosts health checks without raising costs
articles.summary_3_sentences: A University of Manchester study found that social prescribing increased short-term health care use but may reduce primary care visits within a year. The study was published in eClinicalMedicine and reported no cost increase.

articles.title: Q&A: Medicare spending on clinical care for people aging with HIV projected to rise steeply over next decade
articles.summary_3_sentences: Medicare spending on care for Americans aging with HIV is projected to rise from $10.9 billion in 2026 to $27.3 billion in 2035. HIV medications are expected to account for nearly two-thirds of total costs.

articles.title: Cold Storage Sustainability in Federal Labs
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article examines sustainability challenges of maintaining cold storage infrastructure in federal laboratories. It discusses funding constraints and strategies to balance sample preservation with environmental impact.

articles.title: Scientists may have found a way to prevent statin muscle pain
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified an immune response that may contribute to statin-related muscle pain, weakness and exercise intolerance. The finding could eventually support treatments that preserve cardiovascular benefits while protecting muscle.

articles.title: Finerenone Delays Kidney Function Decline
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports clinical data showing finerenone slows kidney function decline in chronic kidney disease. It also notes reduced risk of serious kidney and cardiovascular complications.

articles.title: What's to blame for Canada's wildfires?
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses Canada's wildfires, toxic smoke and misinformation surrounding the causes. It frames wildfires as an ongoing public health and environmental hazard.

articles.title: Scientists discover a hidden heart valve risk linked to gum disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that bacteria associated with gum disease may contribute to calcific aortic valve stenosis by promoting inflammation and calcium buildup. The findings are early and suggest oral health may relate to heart valve risk.

topic_groups.topic: Autoimmune, Inflammatory, Pain and Musculoskeletal Disorders

articles.title: Why the body's inflammatory alarm misfires in familial Mediterranean fever
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article describes research on familial Mediterranean fever, a hereditary autoinflammatory disease caused by MEFV mutations affecting pyrin. It focuses on why the immune system overreacts and produces recurrent fever and inflammation.

articles.title: A drug already used for osteoporosis blocked spinal damage in a new study
articles.summary_3_sentences: Zebrafish with a faulty collagen-related gene developed mineral buildup and spinal fusion resembling human disc disease. Researchers reduced damage with an existing osteoporosis drug and by targeting fat metabolism in the model.

articles.title: Dirty air may trigger painful rheumatoid arthritis flares
articles.summary_3_sentences: Tiny pollution particles from smoke, soot and dust were linked to worsening rheumatoid arthritis and higher flare risk, especially after prolonged exposure. The findings suggest air quality may matter in disease management.

articles.title: Unexpected Roles for a Muscle-Protecting Protein are Revealed
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that TRF2, known for protecting chromosome ends, also has roles in muscle protection. The findings suggest functions beyond its canonical telomere role.

articles.title: Genetic Study of Fibromyalgia Reveals a Surprising Link to Huntington's
articles.summary_3_sentences: A genetic study found an unexpected connection between fibromyalgia and Huntington's disease. The article highlights overlapping genetic risk factors that could inform future therapeutic research.

articles.title: Without this protein, damaged muscle turns to fat and scar tissue
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that TRF2 helps muscle stem cells maintain identity and coordinate repair. Without it, damaged muscle may turn toward fat and scar tissue rather than regeneration.

articles.title: A single sauna session sends immune cells surging
articles.summary_3_sentences: Finnish researchers found that a 30-minute sauna session followed by a short cold shower increased circulating white blood cells. The effect included neutrophils and lymphocytes and was described as brief immune activation.

articles.title: A daily fiber supplement reduced knee arthritis pain and improved strength
articles.summary_3_sentences: A six-week trial found that a prebiotic fiber supplement reduced knee osteoarthritis pain and improved grip strength and pain sensitivity. The findings suggest a possible gut-muscle-pain connection.

articles.title: Exercise may not help hip arthritis as much as patients expect
articles.summary_3_sentences: A major review found exercise produced only small average improvements in hip osteoarthritis pain and function. Researchers noted that evidence is limited on which exercises work best.

articles.title: Natural compound may fight rheumatoid arthritis at its source
articles.summary_3_sentences: A plant-derived compound reduced swelling, inflammation and joint damage in rats with rheumatoid arthritis. It also appeared to rebalance immune activity and fat processing in the preclinical model.

articles.title: Everyday packaging plastic may compound fatty liver risk from burgers and sodas
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found evidence that polyethylene may contribute to fatty liver disease and worsen it when combined with an unhealthy diet. The findings address possible health effects of common plastic exposure.

articles.title: Scientists discover bacteria that lock toxic uranium into a stable form
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers fed microbes in uranium-contaminated mine water with glycerol and observed about 95% of dissolved uranium disappear within 130 days. The bacteria helped convert uranium into an unusually stable compound.

articles.title: Scientists find unexpected life on Ötzi the Iceman's 5,300-year-old body
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers separated microbes associated with Ötzi during life from organisms that arrived after death. They identified traces of original gut bacteria and cold-loving yeasts that may have persisted in the glacier.

articles.title: World's most-used weedkiller disrupts honeybee brains
articles.summary_3_sentences: Glyphosate-exposed honeybees foraged 13% less after three days and showed changes in brain chemicals linked to behavior. The article notes potential hive-level effects on honey production, pollination and survival.

articles.title: The Gut Microbiome is Linked to Memory Formation
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports research showing gut microbes influence memory processes. It describes a causal relationship between microbiome composition and memory performance.

articles.title: Specific Gut Microbes Linked to Changes in Aging Rates
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified gut microbes associated with altered aging rates. The article suggests microbiome-targeted strategies may be explored for healthy aging.

articles.title: Scientists found mystery bacteria inside one of the ocean's most elusive whales
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers studying pygmy sperm whale strandings identified three previously unknown Helicobacter types in whale stomachs. Infected whales had severe digestive damage, but the bacteria were not confirmed as the cause of death.

articles.title: The Power of Bacteria: Cells Render Uranium Inert
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that certain bacteria can render uranium inert. It highlights potential bioremediation applications for managing radioactive contamination.

articles.title: Coffee may help the body fight stress and aging through a hidden cellular switch
articles.summary_3_sentences: Coffee compounds appeared to activate NR4A1, a receptor involved in cellular protection from stress, inflammation and damage. Plant-derived compounds such as caffeic acid appeared more active than caffeine in the reported work.

articles.title: Gut Microbes Work as a Vitamin A Delivery System
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that certain gut bacteria can deliver vitamin A to the host. The finding describes a mechanism of nutrient transport in host-microbe symbiosis.

topic_groups.topic: Genetics, Genomics, Evolution and Basic Biology

articles.title: Telomere-to-telomere brown rat genome could sharpen disease research models
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers created the most complete brown rat genetic profile to date. The telomere-to-telomere genome may improve disease models for conditions such as heart disease, kidney disease, high blood pressure and stroke.

articles.title: Forget the sperm race: Fertilization may depend on teamwork
articles.summary_3_sentences: An evolutionary study found that sperm cooperation is widespread among arthropods and has repeatedly evolved and disappeared. The work challenges the idea that fertilization is always a race among individual sperm.

articles.title: Stanford scientists discover immune cells that explode like microscopic bombs
articles.summary_3_sentences: Stanford researchers found flatworm immune cells that rapidly explode to kill nearby bacteria and foreign cells. The localized response could offer clues for targeted infection or cancer treatment research.

articles.title: Scientists catch a "jumping gene" mid-leap between species
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found circular intron RNA from a predatory bacterium inside dead cells of another microorganism. The stable RNA ring may represent a previously unknown route for mobile genetic elements to move between species.

articles.title: Two deadly flowers could inspire powerful new medicines
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists identified six enzymes used by wolfsbane and larkspur to make atisinium, a medically interesting compound. They recreated the pathway in tobacco plants to support larger-scale production and testing.

articles.title: Scientists found two mysterious 'ghost' ancestors hiding in our DNA
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers report that modern humans carry DNA from two mysterious extinct lineages in addition to Neanderthals and Denisovans. The finding supports a complex history of repeated interbreeding among human groups.

articles.title: Scientists found evolution repeating itself in the Galápagos Islands
articles.summary_3_sentences: Galápagos giant daisies repeatedly evolved similar heat-tolerant leaf shapes using different gene combinations. Researchers also found genetic differences among isolated populations that may indicate ongoing speciation.

articles.title: Surprising Variation in Individual Gene Expression is Discovered
articles.summary_3_sentences: Research found substantial variation in gene expression among individuals over time. The article notes that single-time-point blood samples may miss important dynamics.

articles.title: Hidden genetic diversity helped inbred brown tree snakes conquer guam
articles.summary_3_sentences: Long-read sequencing uncovered more than 19,000 large genetic differences in brown tree snakes, many in immunity and smell genes. This hidden diversity may have helped a small founding population thrive on Guam.

articles.title: Scientists trace the shocking origin of human eyes to an ancient "cyclops"
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers propose that a one-eyed ancestor from nearly 600 million years ago shaped vertebrate eye evolution. They also link its ancient median eye to the modern pineal gland.

articles.title: Scientists discover the hidden brain switch that assigns bees their jobs
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found brain circuits that help determine which jobs worker bees perform as they age. Switching off the circuits caused older bees to resume queen-care behaviors.

articles.title: Koalas nearly went extinct before humans arrived, DNA study reveals
articles.summary_3_sentences: A DNA study found that koalas experienced a major population collapse about 100,000 years ago before humans reached Australia. Researchers calculated the koala mutation rate and analyzed hundreds of genomes.

articles.title: Deep-sea life has a secret food source scientists never expected
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists found that extreme deep-sea pressure can squeeze nutrients out of sinking organic particles. The discovery may change understanding of deep-ocean ecosystems and carbon storage.

topic_groups.topic: Medical Technology, Devices, AI and Research Methods

articles.title: Deep learning refines how bionic eyes communicate with the brain
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers demonstrated that AI may make future visual prostheses more precise, predictable and individualized. The work could improve how bionic eyes communicate with the brain.

articles.title: Barbie and Ken get a reality check after 30 years
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study from Adelaide University and UNSW Sydney found Barbie and Ken have become more physically realistic over time. The article relates to representation and body-image-relevant research.

articles.title: How drugs leach out of your sweat (and can spoil your sofa)
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article explains that medicines can leave the body through sweat or body oils and damage leather furniture. It is a consumer-health explainer about drug residues and materials.

articles.title: Scientists find a simple way to stop cavities without drilling
articles.summary_3_sentences: A major U.S. trial found that silver diamine fluoride stopped decay in more than half of treated baby teeth. The topical treatment requires no drilling, shots or sedation, but darkens decayed areas.

articles.title: Beyond the bead: rethinking small‑scale protein purification
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses alternatives to traditional bead-based small-scale protein purification. It highlights possible improvements in efficiency and scalability for research and process development.

articles.title: 4 in 5 toddler foods are ultra-processed
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Texas grocery-store audit found that 81% of nearly 2,800 toddler foods were ultra-processed. Almost half failed at least one WHO nutrient standard, often due to sugar, sodium, fat or calorie content.

articles.title: Your fingers may hold a secret of human brain evolution
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study of 225 newborns linked finger-length patterns associated with prenatal estrogen exposure to larger head circumference in boys. The same association was not observed in girls.

articles.title: Scientists tracked 12 people in Antarctica for 10 months--what happened could shape future Mars missions
articles.summary_3_sentences: A ten-month Antarctic study found interpersonal tension and cultural or language-based subgrouping in an isolated crew. The findings may inform planning for future Mars missions.

articles.title: Inside the Backrooms: The internet's creepiest place is becoming a tourist attraction
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article describes how the Backrooms evolved from an eerie image into an interactive fictional world built through online media. Researchers interpret its popularity as a form of digital tourism.
